title: Release the shared PDF upload parser after extraction and errors

source.ref: Installed pdf-parse 2.4.5 documents awaited destroy in finally; actual-function recorder reproduced zero cleanup calls, 2026-10-24

detail: The shared Journey, Circle and Spark upload reader constructed PDFParse and returned text without releasing its loaded document. It now awaits destroy in finally for successful, empty and failed reads. The actual-function recorder probe failed before repair (zero cleanup calls) and now passes four PDF resource cases plus unchanged text and Word paths. Three mutation controls (cleanup removed, not awaited and rejection hidden) each produce the intended AssertionError. A generated one-page text PDF and an invalid PDF pass through the installed real parser and actual shared reader; instrumentation confirms awaited real cleanup, cleared doc and preserved caller input. Focused TypeScript with installed Next/Node declarations and lint pass. The first standalone type command omitted project ambient declarations; corrected explicit Next/Node setup passes, with the failed setup log retained. A first real-parser evidence writer tried an unexported package.json path after the parser assertions; the writer now reads installed metadata from the filesystem and the unchanged real cases pass. This establishes parser resource ownership, not a measured RSS/latency gain or broad PDF security certification. No uploaded production files, provider calls, shared data or schema changes. Whole-tree compile integration for this later repair remains pending; the separate audience build runs on878289f3f.

verify.note: Execute actual shared upload reader with bounded local parser recorders, checking awaited cleanup and original error propagation; no database or provider calls.
